title: Guidance and Conviction of the Holy Spirit
definition: The guidance and conviction of the Holy Spirit is His work of leading believers in truth and exposing sin so they may trust Christ and walk in obedience.
summary: The Holy Spirit guides God's people in truth and convicts hearts concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment.
christFocus: Jesus promised that the Spirit would guide into truth, glorify Christ, and convict the world of its need for Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit guides believers according to God's truth. He does not lead contrary to Scripture, glorify self, or promote confusion. His guidance draws attention to Christ and forms obedience to God's Word.

The Spirit also convicts. He exposes sin, reveals the need for righteousness, and presses the heart toward repentance and faith. Conviction is not the same as hopeless condemnation. It is God's gracious work to awaken truth and lead people toward Christ.

Believers need both guidance and conviction. Without guidance, they wander. Without conviction, they excuse sin. The Spirit faithfully works to lead God's people in the way of life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often confuse feelings, impulses, or guilt with the Spirit's leading. This doctrine matters because it teaches believers to test guidance by Scripture and to receive conviction as grace that leads back to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When you sense conviction, do not run from God. Confess sin and obey His Word. When you seek guidance, pray, search Scripture, seek wise counsel, and look for the Spirit's leading to align with Christ's truth.
